source.question: A curve of radius 60 m is banked at 12°. The coefficient of static friction between tyres and road is 0.30. Take g = 9.8 m/s^2. Find the maximum speed at which a car can take the curve without skidding outward, the speed at which no friction is needed, and say whether a car parked on the curve would slide down.

entities.role: limiting static friction down the bank at maximum speed
entities.label: fₛ

annotations.text: At the verge of outward skidding, static friction acts down the bank. v_max = 17.94 m/s.
With no friction needed, v₀ = 11.18 m/s.
A parked car does not slide down: tan 12° ≈ 0.213 is less than μₛ = 0.30. Its static friction would act up the bank.

revealGroups.narrationCue: The car sits on a road banked at 12°.
Show forces for the maximum-speed case; friction points down the bank.
